text: γένοι’ οἷος ἐσσὶ μαθών
translation: Become what you are, once you have learned it.

text: γηράσκω δ’ αἰεὶ πολλὰ διδασκόμενος
translation: I grow old forever learning many things.

text: φύσις κρύπτεσθαι φιλεῖ
translation: Nature loves to hide.

text: ἦθος ἀνθρώπῳ δαίμων
translation: Character is a person's fate.

text: ἔνδον σκάπτε· ἔνδον ἡ πηγὴ τοῦ ἀγαθοῦ
translation: Dig within. Within is the wellspring of the good.

text: πόλλ’ οἶδ’ ἀλώπηξ, ἀλλ’ ἐχῖνος ἓν μέγα
translation: The fox knows many things, the hedgehog one big one.

text: μνάσεσθαί τινά φαῖμι καὶ ἕτερον ἀμμέων
translation: Someone, I say, will remember us in time to come.

text: ὁ βίος βραχύς, ἡ δὲ τέχνη μακρή
translation: Life is short, but the craft is long.

text: οὔτοι ἀπ’ ἀρχῆς πάντα θεοὶ θνητοῖσ’ ὑπέδειξαν, ἀλλὰ χρόνῳ ζητοῦντες ἐφευρίσκουσιν ἄμεινον
translation: The gods did not reveal everything to mortals from the beginning, but in time, by searching, they find out better.

text: μέτρον ἄριστον
translation: Moderation is best.
source: Cleobulus of Lindus, in Diogenes Laertius 1.93

text: Mihi quaestio factus sum.
translation: I have become a question to myself.

text: Vivere militare est.
translation: To live is to keep up the fight.

text: Homines dum docent discunt.
translation: While they teach, people learn.

text: Gutta cavat lapidem, consumitur anulus usu.
translation: The drop hollows the stone; the ring is worn away by use.

text: Dimidium facti qui coepit habet.
translation: Whoever has begun has half the deed done.

text: Possunt quia posse videntur.
translation: They can because they believe they can.

text: Nil sine magno vita labore dedit mortalibus.
translation: Life has given nothing to mortals without great labor.

text: Etiam capillus unus habet umbram suam.
translation: Even a single hair casts its own shadow.

text: Non est ad astra mollis e terris via.
translation: There is no easy road from the earth to the stars.

text: χαλεπὰ τὰ καλά
translation: What is beautiful is hard-won.
source: Greek proverb, in Plato, Hippias Major 304e and Republic 435c

text: Nusquam est, qui ubique est.
translation: One who is everywhere is nowhere.

text: τῆς δ’ ἀρετῆς ἱδρῶτα θεοὶ προπάροιθεν ἔθηκαν ἀθάνατοι
translation: Before excellence the immortal gods have set sweat.

text: ἐσθλῶν μὲν γὰρ ἄπ’ ἐσθλὰ μαθήσεαι
translation: From noble men you will learn noble things.

text: Quae legentem fefellissent, transferentem fugere non possunt.
translation: What might escape a reader cannot escape a translator.

text: μέγα βιβλίον μέγα κακόν
translation: A big book is a big evil.

text: τῇς ἐν μὲν νόος ἐστὶ μετὰ φρεσίν, ἐν δὲ καὶ αὐδὴ καὶ σθένος
translation: In them is mind, and speech, and strength.

text: Ignotas animum dimittit in artes naturamque novat.
translation: He turns his mind to unknown arts and remakes nature.

text: ἐὰν μὴ ἔλπηται, ἀνέλπιστον οὐκ ἐξευρήσει
translation: If you do not hope, you will not find the unhoped-for.

text: Nil mortalibus ardui est.
translation: Nothing is too steep for mortals.

text: πολλῶν δ’ ἀνθρώπων ἴδεν ἄστεα καὶ νόον ἔγνω
translation: He saw the cities of many peoples and learned their minds.

text: Patet omnibus veritas, nondum est occupata.
translation: Truth is open to all; no one has taken it over yet.

text: αἱ κερκίδες ἐκέρκιζον αὐταὶ καὶ τὰ πλῆκτρα ἐκιθάριζεν
translation: The shuttles would weave by themselves, and the picks play the lyre.

text: Ignoranti quem portum petat nullus suus ventus est.
translation: For one who does not know which harbor to seek, no wind is favorable.

text: ἐτεῇ δὲ οὐδὲν ἴδμεν· ἐν βυθῷ γὰρ ἡ ἀλήθεια
translation: In truth we know nothing, for truth lies in the depths.

text: Ratio omnia vincit.
translation: Reason overcomes everything.

text: ὄψις γὰρ τῶν ἀδήλων τὰ φαινόμενα
translation: What appears is a glimpse of what is hidden.

text: Multum adhuc restat operis multumque restabit.
translation: Much work remains, and much will remain.

text: πᾶσαι τέχναι βροτοῖσιν ἐκ Προμηθέως
translation: All the arts of mortals come from Prometheus.

text: καταδύεται εἰς τὸ ἐντὸς τῆς ψυχῆς ὅ τε ῥυθμὸς καὶ ἁρμονία
translation: Rhythm and harmony sink down into the inner depths of the soul.

text: ὄφρά οἱ αὐτόματοι θεῖον δυσαίατ’ ἀγῶνα
translation: So that of their own accord they might enter the gods’ assembly.

text: κτῆμά τε ἐς αἰεὶ μᾶλλον ἢ ἀγώνισμα ἐς τὸ παραχρῆμα
translation: A possession for all time, rather than a showpiece for the moment.

text: ἐδιζησάμην ἐμεωυτόν
translation: I went searching for myself.

text: νᾶφε καὶ μέμνασ’ ἀπιστεῖν· ἄρθρα ταῦτα τᾶν φρενῶν
translation: Stay sober and remember to doubt: these are the joints of the mind.
